title: Slack workspace data (Snap install)
whyItMatters: The Snap version of Slack keeps its own copy of every signed-in workspace, with message cache, files, drafts and the session, under the snap folder rather than ~/.config. It shows which companies the person worked with.
source: Snap keeps per-app data in ~/snap/<name>/<revision>; Slack's Snap uses ~/.config/Slack inside it: https://snapcraft.io/slack and https://slack.com/intl/en-gb/help/articles/360048367814-Update-the-Slack-desktop-app
notes: The * is the snap revision number, not a single fixed folder: after an update snap may keep more than one revision, so this rule can match several and their sizes overlap with what Slack actually uses. ~/snap/slack/current is a symlink, which the path jail refuses to follow, so the revision folder is matched directly. A Flatpak install uses ~/.var/app/com.slack.Slack/config/Slack.

cleanup.signOut: In Slack, click your workspace name in the sidebar and choose Sign out, or sign out all other sessions from your Slack account settings.
steps: Quit Slack from its tray icon.
Uninstall the Slack snap from the App Center or with the Snap Store app.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes the message cache, downloaded files and drafts for every workspace in the snap folder. Workspace data on the servers is untouched.
cleanup.source: Slack Help, Sign out of Slack: https://slack.com/help/articles/214613347-Sign-out-of-Slack
